name: COVID-19
description: A contagious disease caused by the coronavirus SARS-CoV-2. It primarily affects the respiratory system and accesses host cells via the ACE2 receptor.
transmission: Airborne transmission via droplets/aerosols, and contact transmission.

name: Seasonal Influenza
description: An acute respiratory infection caused by influenza viruses. Severity and timing vary by location, influenced by circulating viruses and population immunity.
transmission: Airborne droplets and contact with contaminated surfaces.

name: Dengue Fever
description: A mosquito-borne viral infection causing a severe flu-like illness. Can progress to severe dengue (Dengue Hemorrhagic Fever) causing bleeding and blood plasma leakage.

name: Malaria
description: A life-threatening disease caused by Plasmodium parasites (e.g., P. falciparum, P. vivax) transmitted to people through the bites of infected female Anopheles mosquitoes.

name: Ebola Virus Disease
description: A rare but severe, often fatal illness in humans caused by Ebola virus (family Filoviridae). Outbreaks occur primarily in tropical regions of sub-Saharan Africa.
transmission: Direct contact with blood, secretions, organs, or other bodily fluids of infected people or animals.

name: Tuberculosis
description: An infectious disease caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis bacteria that most often affects the lungs. It is the world's second leading infectious killer after COVID-19.
transmission: Airborne via respiratory droplets when infected persons cough, sneeze, or spit.

name: HIV/AIDS
description: Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) attacks the body's immune system. If not treated, it can lead to AIDS (Acquired Immunodeficiency Syndrome). No effective cure exists, but with proper treatment, HIV can be controlled.
transmission: Through exchange of certain body fluids: blood, breast milk, semen, and vaginal secretions.

name: Cholera
description: An acute diarrhoeal infection caused by ingestion of food or water contaminated with Vibrio cholerae bacterium. Cholera remains a global threat to public health and an indicator of inequity and lack of social development.
transmission: Fecal-oral route through contaminated water and food.

name: Mpox
description: A viral zoonotic disease caused by Monkeypox virus (MPXV), belonging to the Orthopoxvirus genus. In 2022-2024, a multi-country outbreak spread globally beyond its traditional endemic regions in Africa.
transmission: Close physical contact with infected persons, contaminated materials, or infected animals.

name: Measles
description: A highly contagious viral disease caused by the Morbillivirus. Despite the availability of a safe and effective vaccine, measles remains one of the leading causes of death among young children globally.
transmission: Airborne via respiratory droplets and aerosolized particles. Extremely contagious.
